after: **Simplifications:** rigid, massless arms and links; point-mass balls; frictionless joints and sleeve; no throttle load; constant imposed speed. At balance, g·tanθ = ω²(e + L·sinθ). Below lift-off speed the sleeve rests on the lower collar, and above the upper limit it is blocked by the upper collar. Playback adds a light damping term so the arms settle. This is a teaching model, not a load-rated engineering simulation.
title: Centrifugal governor · balance in motion
before: A centrifugal governor turns **speed into position**. As the spindle spins faster, the balls swing outward on hinged arms of fixed length, and the links pull the sliding sleeve up the spindle. That sleeve travel would normally move a throttle lever.
caption: Isometric two-ball Watt-type governor. Hinged arms of fixed length carry the balls; clevis links tie each arm to a sleeve that slides on the vertical spindle between two stop collars. Change the speed to see the arms open and the sleeve rise.
